cards.text: In the book of Isaiah, the LORD's Servant speaks up. His first words are "Listen to Me…" and He's calling out to someone in particular.

cards.question: The LORD's Servant calls out for people to listen to Him. Who is He calling?

cards.text: He says the LORD called Him from the womb and named Him from His mother's body. Me? I sat at the bottom of a closing bakery's last bin with a 25-CENT sticker on me before anybody carved my name.
Then He says the LORD made His mouth like a sharp sword and hid Him in the shadow of His hand.

cards.question: The LORD made His Servant like a polished arrow and hid Him in His ___.

cards.text: Then the Servant says the LORD told Him, "You are My Servant, Israel…" And the LORD says He'll put something of His own on display in Him.

cards.question: The LORD tells His Servant that He will display His glory in Him.

cards.text: Then the Servant says what He answered: He's labored in vain and spent His strength in futility. Friend, back when I was a worn-out old cookie stamper, I gave every batch EVERYTHING, and the cookies still came out looking like they were stamped during an EARTHQUAKE.

cards.question: Even after saying His work was in vain, the Servant says His reward is with His ___.

cards.text: Then the Servant says the LORD formed Him from the womb to be His Servant, to bring Jacob back to the LORD so Israel might be gathered to Him.

cards.question: The Servant also says something about how the LORD sees Him. What is it?

answers.text: He is honored in the LORD's sight
He is a stranger to the LORD
He is out of the LORD's favor

cards.text: Then the LORD says it's not enough for His Servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and restore the protected ones of Israel. Baker, if somebody told me ONE oven of cookies was not enough, I'd need to sit down on my gold base for a WHILE.

cards.question: Raising up Jacob's tribes isn't enough. What else will the LORD make His Servant?

cards.text: Through His Servant, the LORD's salvation will reach the ends of the earth. Now the LORD, the Redeemer and Holy One of Israel, speaks to the One the nation despised and abhorred, the Servant of rulers.

cards.question: When kings see the despised Servant, they will rise, and princes will ___.
Kings and princes will honor the Servant because of the great army He leads.

cards.text: The LORD keeps speaking. In the time of favor, He says, He'll answer His Servant.

cards.question: In the day of salvation, the LORD will ___ His Servant.

cards.text: The LORD will also keep Him and appoint Him to be a covenant for the people, to restore the land and divide up its desolate inheritances. That's a BIG to-do list, and I lose my ONE little list in my apron pocket every single day.

cards.question: The Servant is also appointed to say something to the prisoners. What is it?

cards.text: And to those in darkness, He'll say, "Show yourselves." Friend, I spent years in the back of a dark junk drawer, holding my breath every time it opened, hoping somebody would say just that.
Then the picture changes. The people coming out will feed along the pathways and find pasture on every barren hill.

cards.question: Along the way, the people coming out will still go hungry and thirsty.
No scorching heat or sun will beat down on the people coming out. Where will the One guiding them lead them?

cards.text: Then the LORD says He'll turn all His mountains into roads, and His highways will be raised up. Friend, folks groan when ONE orange cone shows up on the highway, and here the MOUNTAINS are getting out of the way!

cards.question: Then the LORD says to look. Something is on the way. What is it?

cards.text: Those people will come from the north, from the west, and from the land of Aswan.
Then the heavens are told to shout for joy, the earth to rejoice, and the mountains to break forth in song. MOUNTAINS singing, friend, and I can't even get my oven timer to beep on key.

cards.question: The heavens, the earth and the mountains are told to celebrate because the LORD has comforted His people.
The passage ends with a promise: the LORD will show ___ to His afflicted ones.
